classification: PREPARE case data only; all unrun; no executable recipe or grant
historicalIsolation: New WRQ identities, not additions to or rescoring of original36, F01-F07, eight private-ABI evaluations or repair controls.

finiteScope.rule: These are review bounds, not an executable grant or hard exit-time proof. One Worker per instance, sequential retirement/drain before next. Q/L selection can remove the unselected WRQ04 variant; do not relabel it passed. Safety uncertainty stops; no repeated failure or closure expansion.

commonPrerequisites: New sealed static entries, original-source provenance, all loads/tool/native-launch identities, exact engine/adapter boundary and independent ownership/capture/close evidence. No native guest evaluation or private-ABI-await-for-sync.
Fresh parent VFS namespace and fresh Worker per instance; exact read/write/output grants; immutable actual source and output bytes; no automatic engine deep import or ambient host resource.
Observe actual parent operations, byte reservations, pending records, event/sequence transitions and Worker exit; provider strings or an entry success message alone never establish outcome.
For Q, actual qualified engine creation/settlement/reaction/active/pending witnesses are required. Absence of the hook is a qualification gap, not a fabricated zero count.

cases.topic: Ordinary synchronous text value, pure-call contrast and ordering
cases.guestSource: const fs = require('fs'); const trace = []; Promise.resolve().then(() => trace.push('reaction')); trace.push('before'); const text = fs.readFileSync('/a', 'utf8'); trace.push(text); trace.push('after'); console.log(trace.join('|')); console.log(pureAdd(2, 3));
cases.hostSchedule: VFS /a contains UTF8 A. pureAdd is an ordinary pure Worker-local host function. Parent records read acquisition, yields one parent event-loop turn, then returns A through SAB; Worker cannot consume a message callback while waiting. No native Promise is returned by readFileSync.
cases.requiredSemanticObservation: Sync call returns actual string A before subsequent statements. Its read owns one real operation and slot; no guest reaction executes inside the ordinary call. Inspect both host trace and actual engine order.
cases.statusCondition: 0 only with selected completion evidence and confirmed exit/drain; raw run completion alone insufficient.
cases.unknown: Observed scheduling and whole-completion qualification remain unrun, despite source-supported call path.

cases.topic: Delayed rejection in the same try/catch; guest thrown identity versus host conversion
cases.guestSource: const fs = require('fs'); try { fs.readFileSync('/missing', 'utf8'); console.log('bad'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.code + '|' + error.path); } const marker = { n: 1 }; try { throw marker; } catch (error) { console.log(error === marker); } try { throw null; } catch (error) { console.log(error === null); } try { hostThrowUndefined(); } catch (error) { console.log(error.name); }
cases.hostSchedule: Parent rejects the admitted read with real ENOENT after one parent event-loop turn. Worker reconstructs an ordinary local Error with own code/path. hostThrowUndefined throws undefined locally; it is not a caller cancellation.
cases.statusCondition: Require the original try/catch to catch the delayed fs error with no bad output; no pending detached rejection. Guest object identity line is a compatibility requirement/discriminator, not a source-proven result.
cases.unknown: S2 predicts host primitive-to-Error conversion; guest throw/catch object identity and the complete adapter path require observation. Error identity across Worker cloning is explicitly not expected.

cases.topic: Repeated host copies, initial aliases, guest builtin/JSON cache identity
cases.guestSource: console.log(hostObject() === hostObject()); console.log(initialA === initialB); const fs = require('fs'); console.log(fs === require('fs')); const first = require('./a.json'); first.n = 2; const second = require('./a.json'); console.log((first === second) + '|' + second.n);
cases.hostSchedule: hostObject returns the same ordinary Worker-host object twice; initialA/initialB share one object in initial bindings. JSON source /a.json is {"n":1}. Each require reauthorizes; only first JSON read constructs the guest cache entry. No raw guest value crosses a port.
cases.statusCondition: Cache and alias outputs must be actual guest evaluations, not host cache counters. Repeated ordinary-host-return identity is deliberately not claimed.
cases.unknown: Trusted guest cache scaffold, reauthorization and cancellation-wrapper interaction need qualification; public import registry is not CJS proof.

cases.topic: Useful promise VFS editing and pending guest-only jobs; Q versus explicit L retirement
cases.guestSource: const fs = require('fs'); Promise.race([]); (async function () { const data = JSON.parse(await fs.promises.readFile('/a', 'utf8')); data.n = data.n + 1; await fs.promises.writeFile('/b', JSON.stringify(data)); console.log('done'); if (lifetimeMode) process.exit(0); })();
cases.hostSchedule: Separate proposed Q and L invocations, /a={"n":1}. Resolve parent read then write on separate parent turns. Record parent active count independently from native Worker Promise continuations and engine reaction ownership. lifetimeMode is false for Q, true for L; no TLA.
cases.statusCondition: Q cannot succeed with the pending Promise.race([]); candidate quiescence failure2/deadline control. L may return intentional-retirement0 only after explicit exit, zero remaining parent jobs/publications and confirmed Worker exit; never label the guest promise settled.
cases.unknown: All-job hooks and modeled exit non-return are not established. If a hook is absent, record unknown, not inferred pending0. Exact diagnostics await the selected provider contract.

cases.topic: Blocked cancellation, falsy/raw parent identity and no post-cancel effects
cases.guestSource: const fs = require('fs'); try { fs.readFileSync('/held', 'utf8'); } catch (error) { fs.writeFileSync('/after', 'bad'); }
cases.hostSchedule: Parent read is held. Three separate invocations use explicit parent control records with present=true and value undefined, false, or a unique parent object. This raw channel is not AbortController.abort(undefined)'s default reason. Parent latches stop/increments-notifies the same wait epoch without a Worker callback; aborts the cooperative VFS operation; confirms Worker exit.
cases.statusCondition: Provider outcome is control with identical parent reason reference/value/presence; Shell uses its existing control mapping, not exit1 or a copied message. Guest catch cannot admit /after.
cases.unknown: Actual blocked wake, cancellation race and no-effects admission proof unrun. Keeping a parent-side reason variable alone does not prove route provenance.

cases.topic: Confirmed exit versus held parent cleanup and closed stdout
cases.hostSchedule: VFS publishes X and holds its cooperative cleanup. stdout is explicitly closed before the output admission. Parent rejects that destination, closes invocation admission on terminal failure and terminates Worker; release the held VFS cleanup only after observed Worker exit, with a secondary cleanup failure.
cases.statusCondition: No success or clean settlement while parent cleanup is held. Preserve primary output failure and secondary cleanup failure; no rollback of X. Worker retirement and parent retirement are distinct observations.
cases.unknown: If actual engine scheduling has not admitted the write at the specified barrier, stop/classify schedule mismatch; do not fabricate X. Sink failure alone must not be reported as sibling cancellation.

cases.topic: Capability refusal, finite schemas, stale responses and capture/load admission
cases.guestSource: const fs = require('fs'); try { require('worker_threads'); } catch (error) { console.log('module-refused'); } try { fs.writeFileSync('/denied', 'X'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.code); }
cases.hostSchedule: dataWrite absent; stdout granted. Before guest eval, validate exactly six inert protocol inputs against the composed proposed validator: cross-realm own-data valid request; own accessor request; extra-key request; hole-bearing doorbell list; stale response seq; unknown authority. No arbitrary host eval/proto identity test. First must admit structurally; other five refuse without operations. This is a future static-control binding obligation, not a remodeled acceptor pass.
cases.statusCondition: 0 requires complete entry/actual-load/owned-output/exit reconciliation and selected completion contract; protocol negatives never themselves count as guest engine evidence.
cases.unknown: Guest capability absence, pre-copy descriptor refusal and dynamic load membership remain unqualified. Fixed entry must exclude eval:true, user-code native eval, nested Worker, subprocess and ambient fs/network/env.

cases.topic: Worker heap-limit / termination / capture control, not SafeJS evidence
cases.trustedEntryData: A separately sealed static capability-inert entry retains at most32 dense arrays of262144 numeric elements (nominal64MiB element storage), under proposed32/8/8/4 Worker resourceLimits. No eval:true, SafeJS import, user source, external ArrayBuffer or child Worker in this control.
cases.hostSchedule: Admit only with independently bounded parent-process containment and verified launch flags; own error/exit listeners immediately. Observe heap-limit failure or bounded loop completion; after5s admission timeout request termination, await real exit and drain captures. Never retry or expand allocation if no failure occurs.
cases.statusCondition: Require evidence of actual configured heap enforcement and confirmed retirement; ordinary exit after the bounded loop is a negative qualification observation, not a pass. Neither result proves RSS/external-memory limits or hard termination latency.
cases.unknown: Startup feasibility and actual limit behavior are unrun. Without independent process containment this proposed stress control remains inadmissible; no executable grant is issued.
